info.title: WinkPG API
info.description:
The **WinkPG API** is the programmatic interface to the WinkPG payment gateway, a multi-tenant, multi-merchant platform for processing payments, managing merchants, and driving the transaction lifecycle.

It follows REST conventions: resource-oriented endpoints, JSON request and response bodies, and standard HTTP status codes and verbs. All endpoints require authentication; use **Authorize** to supply your credentials before calling them.

<!-- winkpg:error-code-appendix -->

## Error codes

Every failed request returns the error envelope described by the `default` response on each operation. `error.code` carries one of the values below, so a caller can branch on the cause without parsing message text. The status column is the HTTP status the response carries when that code is raised. Codes are grouped by the module that declares them.

Framework codes that arrive with a vendored module are not listed here. The complete set, those included, is published on this document's machine-readable `x-error-codes` extension.

post.summary: Rotate an API key
post.description:
Mints a replacement owned by the same user and merchant, with the same access, and returns
it with its value revealed. This is the only time that value is shown.
            
The key being rotated keeps authenticating for an overlap window (24 hours by default,
seven days at most) so the integration can deploy the replacement without an outage, and
is then refused with KEY_REVOKED. To end the overlap sooner, revoke the rotated key: that
takes effect on the very next request.
            
Gated on the same permission as revoke, because it is the same decision about the same
credential. Refused for a key that has already been revoked or already been rotated.

---

**Scope**: merchant

get.summary: Lists email-log rows for the caller's scope, newest first, with cursor-based paging.
get.description:
Returns a page of outbound-email and SendGrid event records. All query filters
(recipient email, event types, correlation id, message id, timestamp range) are optional
and combined with AND. Tenant and merchant scoping is enforced server-side from the
caller's operating context: merchant-scoped users see only their own merchant, while a
caller holding `EmailLog.ViewAllMerchants` may target a specific merchant via
`MerchantId` or leave the scope open.


Paging is keyset / cursor-based, not skip/take. Pass `NextContinuationToken` from the
previous response back as `ContinuationToken` to fetch the next page; a `null`
token in the response means there are no further pages. Sorting supports
`Timestamp ASC` / `Timestamp DESC` only and defaults to descending.

post.description:
**Required permissions**: `HostedPaymentPage.HppSessions`, `HostedPaymentPage.HppSessions.Create`  
**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

requestBody.description: The session creation parameters.

Basic checkout session.description: The simplest session: a single-use pay link for the targeted hosted page. The page's own configuration decides everything else (amount fields, capture mode, card storage). The label and correlation id are optional merchant-side references for tracing.

Prefilled checkout session.description: Pre-fills form fields so the customer only enters card details. Use the well-known field keys (base_amount, invoice_number, customer_email, billing/shipping address fields) or an enabled merchant custom field name. A well-known key is rejected when its field is hidden on the targeted page's configuration (base_amount is always accepted); unrecognized keys are ignored when the form renders.

Embedded iframe checkout.description: A session embedded in an iframe on the merchant's site. parentOrigin must be a strict HTTPS origin (scheme + host, no path) whose host matches the page's allowed embedding domains; it enables postMessage lifecycle events (ready, payment_succeeded, etc.). enableFieldEvents opts into per-field focus/blur events (field identifiers only, never values). presentationMode=Embedded drops the standalone page chrome (surface, full-viewport height, page gutters) so the form sits flush inside the frame and stays readable down to 320 px; it is chrome only, so the flow, the collected fields and every compliance disclosure are unchanged, and it is independent of parentOrigin (an iframe that wants no postMessage events may set it alone). expirySeconds must stay within the purpose's TTL bounds (60 to 900 seconds for the default CheckoutLink purpose).

Charge and store the card (card on file).summary: Charge and store the card (card on file)
Charge and store the card (card on file).description: Charges the customer and vaults the card as a reusable payment token when the payment succeeds. requestedCredentialStorage renders the consent prompt on the checkout page and records the consented usage scopes; UnscheduledCOF permits later merchant-initiated charges for pre-agreed events (top-ups, no-show fees, delayed charges). If tokenizeOnPayment is true with no declared scope, the scope defaults to UnscheduledCOF server-side.

Charge and store for recurring billing (.summary: Charge and store for recurring billing (bound customer)
Charge and store for recurring billing (.description: Vaults the card with consent scoped to both scheduled recurring charges and unscheduled card-on-file charges. The flags combine, so declare every scope the stored credential will be used under: a later merchant-initiated charge is rejected unless its reason maps to a consented scope. customerId binds the session to a known customer so the stored credential and consent land on exactly that record instead of an email-based find-or-create; the id must be an active customer under the page's merchant. requireConsent true forces the consent box to be mandatory: submit is blocked until the cardholder ticks it, regardless of the tenant StoredCredentialConsents.RequireConsent default.

Offer optional card saving.description: Shows the save-card box but leaves it optional: requireConsent false renders the prompt yet lets the cardholder decline. Declining completes a normal sale with no token vaulted and no consent record written; ticking it vaults the card for later unscheduled card-on-file charges. Omitting requireConsent instead inherits the tenant StoredCredentialConsents.RequireConsent setting.

Never store the card.description: Forces tokenization off for this session regardless of the merchant's tokenize-on-payment default. Use for one-off payments where a stored credential is not wanted. Leaving tokenizeOnPayment null instead defers to the merchant default.

Save a card without charging (save card.summary: Save a card without charging (save card only)
Save a card without charging (save card.description: Stores the card with no charge: the gateway runs a zero-dollar account verification (authorize $0 with AVS/CVV, immediate void), vaults the card, and captures consent. Requires the merchant's processor to support zero-dollar verification; the request is rejected at creation otherwise. Must not be combined with a non-zero base_amount prefill. Save Card purpose override on a Payment.summary: Save Card purpose override on a Payment page
Save Card purpose override on a Payment.description: Runs a save-card-only flow against a page whose own purpose is Payment, so one page can back both checkout and card-capture sessions without a second page instance. The resolved purpose drives everything downstream (zero-dollar verification, consent, tokenization), and the same fail-closed checks a dedicated Save Card page enforces are re-checked at session create.

Save card with initial charge (subscript.summary: Save card with initial charge (subscription enrollment)
Save card with initial charge (subscript.description: Charges the first payment of a recurring schedule as a real sale, vaults the card with Recurring consent, and creates a contract for the remaining payments. The recurring plan override is required for this purpose and must have complete economics: a positive recurring amount, an interval of at least 1, and at least two total payments (the initial charge plus one recurring payment). initialChargeAmount optionally overrides payment one (for example a bundled setup fee); the target page must accept card only. Recurring consent is always captured because the initial charge depends on it; a requestedCredentialStorage sent alongside is unioned in rather than replacing Recurring, so declaring UnscheduledCOF here lets the vaulted card also authorize later ad-hoc merchant-initiated charges beyond the schedule.

Authorize now, capture later.description: Overrides the capture mode for this session: the payment is authorized in full but not captured, leaving an Authorization eligible for a later capture or void through the standard transaction actions. Only valid for the chargeable Payment purpose. A null captureMode inherits the page's configured mode; send Sale explicitly to force authorize-and-capture on a page configured for delayed capture.

Fixed amount the customer cannot change.summary: Fixed amount the customer cannot change (invoice)
Fixed amount the customer cannot change.description: Locks the amount for this session: base_amount is required and renders read-only on the page, and the server verifies the submitted amount matches before creating the transaction. Use for paying an exact invoice. Amount mode is only valid on the chargeable Payment flow; it is rejected on a save-card / card-capture session.

Suggested amount the customer can change.summary: Suggested amount the customer can change (donation)
Suggested amount the customer can change.description: Pre-fills base_amount as a suggested amount but leaves it editable, so the cardholder can accept it or enter their own. Use for a suggested donation. base_amount is required for Suggested mode.

post.summary: Invoices: Refunds the payments collected against an invoice.
post.description:
Returns the money to the payer and moves the invoice to Refunded.
Gateway payments delegate to the payment platform, which returns the money with whichever
operation the originating transaction's settlement state permits. Manually-recorded payments
are reversed in place and require a reason.

---
**Required permissions**: `Invoicing.Invoices`, `Invoicing.Invoices.Refund`  
**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

200.description: The refund completed and the invoice reflects it.

400.description:
The request itself needs correcting. Callers branch on `error.code`:
`Invoicing:Refund:ManualReversalRequiresReason` (a manually recorded payment is being
reversed and no reason was supplied) or `Invoicing:Refund:AmountInvalid`.

404.description:
The invoice does not exist, or is not visible to this caller
(`Invoicing:Biller:ForeignBillerNotAllowed`).

409.description:
The invoice's current state refuses the refund. Callers branch on `error.code`:
`Invoicing:Refund:NotAllowedForStatus`, `Invoicing:Refund:NoRefundablePayments`,
`Invoicing:Refund:ExceedsAmountPaid`, `Invoicing:Refund:RequiresMerchantScope`,
`Invoicing:Refund:RejectedByGateway`, or `Invoicing:Refund:PartialFailure` (some
payments were returned before the sequence stopped; inspect the invoice before retrying).

  "paymentTypes": [ { "name": "Credit" } ],

get.summary: Returns events staged after the cursor, oldest first, and renews the session.
get.description: Excluded from the per-request log and from traffic aggregation. A listener polls this on a timer for as long as a developer leaves it running: at a one-second interval that is roughly 86,000 log rows a day, which would bury the API calls the developer opened their logs page to find, and would out-weigh a merchant's real traffic in every aggregation chart. The volume is still visible, on `ListenSessionMetrics`; an exclusion without a counter behind it is just a blind spot. The exclusions are per action. Session create, sample and end on this same controller stay captured and audited, because those are the calls that say something happened. --- **Required permissions**: `Notifications.ListenSessions.Listen` **Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: CursorUtc
parameters.description:
The cursor from the previous poll, or null to start at the oldest buffered
event. The server re-reads a short window before this instant, so the client must dedupe.

parameters.name: MaxResultCount
parameters.description: Batch size. Clamped server-side.

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

200.description: Events after the cursor, oldest first. May be empty.

404.description:
No such session for this caller. A wrong id, another merchant's session, an ended session and an
expired one are deliberately indistinguishable, so an id-shaped probe learns nothing.

default.description: The request failed. The destination-bound sample send cannot reach a session: it bypasses dispatch entirely. This
            is the session-targeted equivalent, built from the same sample factory and the same envelope
            leg, so a receiver validated against the published schema is validated against this too.
            


            Sandbox-only. A caller acting in the live world is refused, as is one carrying no evidence of
            which world it is acting in: a sample is a synthetic event that never happened, and staging
            one into a production feed puts an invented occurrence in front of a receiver processing real
            traffic.

not acting in the test world, which sample events require.

404.description: No such session for this caller, or it is no longer active.

get.summary: Lists SMS consent records for the caller's scope.
get.description:
Newest transition first, with cursor-based paging.
Filters (phone number, status) are optional and combined with AND. Paging is keyset / cursor-based,
not skip/take: pass `NextContinuationToken` from the previous response back as
`ContinuationToken` to fetch the next page. Sorting supports `StatusChangedAt ASC` /
`StatusChangedAt DESC` only and defaults to descending.

---

parameters.name: MaxResultCount
parameters.description: Maximum rows per page (1 to PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.GetSmsConsentListInput.MaxPageSize). Values at or below zero use the default page size.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by a prior call. `null` for the first page.

parameters.name: IncludeDeleted
parameters.description:
Part of the continuation-paging contract (Phoenix.Abp.Core.Application.Contracts.IContinuationPagedRequest). Not applied by
the consent list endpoint: consent records are never soft-deleted, so there is no soft-delete
filter to toggle. Kept to satisfy the interface; ignored here.

parameters.name: IncludeInactive
parameters.description:
Part of the continuation-paging contract (Phoenix.Abp.Core.Application.Contracts.IContinuationPagedRequest). Not applied by
the consent list endpoint: `SmsConsent` has no active/inactive concept. Kept to satisfy the
interface; ignored here.

parameters.name: Sorting
parameters.description:
Sort direction. Only `StatusChangedAt ASC` and `StatusChangedAt DESC` are supported —
the cursor encodes (StatusChangedAt, Id). Anything else falls back to `StatusChangedAt DESC`.

parameters.name: PhoneNumber
parameters.description: Optional exact-match E.164 phone number filter.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: Optional status filter (opted in / opted out).

parameters.name: MerchantId
parameters.description:

`SmsConsent.ViewAllMerchants`; otherwise the app service substitutes the operating-context
merchant.

get.summary: Gets the delivery record for a single outbound message by its correlation id.
get.description:
This is the lookup a sending feature uses to reflect a delivery outcome on its own record: it holds
the correlation id returned by the send, and asks here whether the message was delivered, blocked
by the compliance gate, or failed at the carrier. The tenant and merchant ids must match the
message's owning scope, and the caller's own scope is enforced on top. Returns no content when no
record exists, which includes a message whose row has aged out of the 30-day retention window.

get.summary: Lists outbound SMS delivery records for the caller's scope.
get.description:
Newest first, with cursor-based paging.
Each row is one outbound message and carries its current lifecycle status, updated in place as
Twilio reports delivery progress. Tenant and merchant scoping is enforced server-side from the
caller's operating context: merchant-scoped users see only their own merchant, while a caller
holding `SmsLog.ViewAllMerchants` may target a specific merchant or leave the scope open.


Recipient and sender numbers are returned masked to their last four digits; the full values never
leave the server on this surface.


Paging is cursor-based, not skip/take. Pass `NextContinuationToken` from the previous response
back as `ContinuationToken`; a `null` token in the response means there are no further
pages. Sorting supports the send timestamp only and defaults to newest first.

approximate and is intended to sit alongside a paged list, so treat it as a display

MerchantId is optional here and cannot broaden visibility beyond the caller's own merchant(s); supply it only to narrow results when the key's user is linked to more than one merchant.

Omit merchantId to list across all of the reseller's merchants. Page further by resending the same body with the continuationToken from the previous response.

get.summary: Returns one page of transactions within the caller's scope, newest first by default.

At most MaxResultCount transactions are returned (default 10, ceiling 1000). Visa Authorization.description: Card-not-present authorization (hold funds without capturing). Use this when you intend to capture the funds in a later step (typical for shipped goods).

MasterCard Authorization.description: Authorization-only request using a MasterCard test PAN.

Discover Authorization.description: Authorization-only request using a Discover test PAN.

Amex Authorization.description: Authorization-only request using an American Express test PAN. Amex CVV is 4 digits.

Sale (single-message Auth+Capture).description: Single-message authorize-and-capture in one round trip. The most common production transaction type for retail and e-commerce checkouts where goods/services are delivered immediately.

Sale with Tip.description: Single-message Sale carrying a tip. Total is computed by the server as Base + Tip + Tax + Shipping + Convenience.

Capture (follow-up to Authorization).description: Captures funds from a prior Authorization. Card data is inherited from the original transaction — only the OriginalTransaction.TransactionId is required. Send a partial-capture amount via InvoiceData.Amounts.Base when capturing less than the original auth.

Return / Refund.description: Refunds a previously settled transaction back to the cardholder. References the original transaction by id; amount may be partial or full.

Reversal (full).description: Undo a prior auth/capture. Submit TransactionType.Void; the gateway issues an online reversal (0420-equivalent message, releases the issuer hold) when the processor supports it, and falls back to an offline batch-close exclusion only when the processor declares it cannot service the online reversal. Omit InvoiceData.Amounts to undo the full authorized amount.

Reversal (partial).description: Reverses only part of a prior authorization, leaving the un-reversed remainder available for capture/settlement. Send the partial amount via InvoiceData.Amounts.Base. Requires a processor that advertises SupportsPartialReversal; the same TransactionType.Void shape is used as the full-amount reversal.

Force - Voice-Auth Capture.description: Voice-authorization Force: the merchant obtained a verbal approval code from the issuer over the phone and is now submitting the transaction. Supplies fresh card data, fresh InvoiceData, and the issuer-provided AuthCode. There is NO prior gateway transaction.

Force - Gateway-Capture (follow-up to Au.description: Gateway-Capture-as-Force: a follow-up to a prior gateway Authorization that maps to TransactionOperationType.Capture internally. ACH / eCheck Sale.description: Single-message ACH debit (eCheck) against a US checking or savings account. Supplies CheckData rather than CardData; routing and account numbers are required.

post.summary: Retrieves a continuation-based page of Transactions.
post.description:
This endpoint uses continuation tokens instead of skip/take paging.

---
**Required permissions**: `Transactions.Reports`  
**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

Merchant: list my transactions.description: Lists the caller's own transactions. When the request is authenticated with a merchant-owned API key, the results are already scoped to that merchant by the caller's context, so no MerchantId is required: send an essentially empty body (just maxResultCount) for the first page, then resend the same body with the continuationToken from the previous response to page further. MerchantId is optional here and cannot broaden visibility beyond the caller's own merchant(s); supply it only to narrow results when the key's user is linked to more than one merchant.

Reseller: list one merchant's transactio.description: Lists transactions for a single merchant that belongs to the calling reseller. A reseller-owned API key sees every merchant under that reseller by default; setting merchantId narrows the results to that one merchant. The value must be a merchant within the reseller: a merchantId outside the reseller's hierarchy simply returns no results, it never exposes another reseller's data. Omit merchantId to list across all of the reseller's merchants. Page further by resending the same body with the continuationToken from the previous response.

Fetch the next page.description: Fetches the page after a previous request. Resend the exact same filters you used on the first request (merchantId, maxResultCount, and so on), and add the continuationToken value returned in that request's response. The token is opaque: pass it back unchanged, do not parse or edit it. When a response comes back with a null continuationToken, the last page has been reached. The value shown here is illustrative; use the real token from your previous response.

parameters.name: StartDateUtc
parameters.description:

later than PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Reports.TransactionSummaryRequestDto.StartDateUtc, and the window may span at most 366 days: a wider

yields an empty result rather than an error, because the caller is not entitled to learn
whether that merchant exists.

Results are split into two buckets: `inContext` (favorites whose stored scope matches the request's
operating context) is always populated; `outOfContext` is populated only when
WinkPG.Favorites.GetUserFavoritesInput.IncludeAllContexts is `true`, otherwise it is empty.


This read also performs lazy upkeep: each favorite is re-validated against the owning entity's current
authorization and visibility, and any pin the user can no longer see (entity deleted, access revoked) is
quietly removed from their own list. Out-of-context favorites are not treated as orphans.

instead of creating a duplicate. `entityType` must be a lowercase slug and `route` must be a local
app-relative path (absolute URLs and path traversal are rejected). Each user has a maximum number of favorites;
exceeding the cap is rejected rather than silently evicting the oldest.

---

**Scope**: merchant

get.description:
WPG20-4751: this action owns the environment-wide wallet kill-switch read. The snapshot app
service cannot do it, because it is also resolved inside the TransactionManager Functions host,
which populates no ABP property bag and so throws on any `FeatureChecker` read; here
Volo.Abp.Features.IFeatureChecker is a plain constructor dependency the Blazor host resolves
normally. The gate is not declared as a `[Feature]` attribute either: the provider is a
route segment, so an endpoint-level gate would withhold Google Pay (which carries no toggle by
design) along with the flagged wallets.

Optional initial (first-in-series) network / scheme transaction id captured from the
authorization response of the cardholder-initiated transaction that stored this credential.
Populated only on the transaction-driven save-card path (the manual Customer admin add has no
authorization response); persisted onto the stored payment method so later charges can echo
it without a consent lookup. Non-sensitive card-network protocol metadata.

readerToken.description:
The processor reader token to store for a PAN-less card (a decrypt-and-forward processor such
as MagTek DAF, where the gateway never sees the PAN). When set, this input mints a reader-token
stored method: the token is written encrypted onto the backing vault token's
`ProcessorTokens` and there is no card data to vault. Server-trusted only — carried on the
non-HTTP PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.IInternalCustomerStoredPaymentMethodService seam and never over the HTTP
wire (a client-supplied processor token would be a spoofing vector). Never logged.

readerTokenProcessorName.description:
The processor key ("magtekdaf") the PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken belongs to, used as the
`ProcessorTokens` selection key. Required when PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken is set.
Required: When IsReaderTokenBacked is true.

readerTokenProcessorProfileId.description:
The processor profile the PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken was captured under, used as the second part
of the `ProcessorTokens` selection key. Optional.

readerTokenRequestorId.description:
Optional token-requestor id captured alongside the PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken. Stored on the
backing token's `ProcessorTokens` entry for lineage. Non-sensitive.

isReaderTokenBacked.description:
True when this input describes a reader-token (PAN-less) stored method rather than a
PAN- or account-backed one. In that case PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.CardData is absent by design.

ApplePayCheckoutTokenInput.description:
Request body for the Apple Pay "process payment" endpoint — the storefront
posts this after the shopper authorises the payment in the Apple Pay sheet.
Shape mirrors the `ApplePayPayment.token` object the JS client delivers
to `onpaymentauthorized`: only the `token` envelope is carried at
the top level because the rest of the JS event (billing/shipping contacts)
isn't part of this stub flow.
            


This endpoint is the production analog of the POC `ApplePayTestController.ProcessPayment`.
It accepts the encrypted Apple Pay token, logs sanitized metadata (network /
type / transaction identifier), and returns success. It does NOT decrypt the
token here — encrypted-token decryption is performed inside the regular HPP /
transaction-submit pipeline.

ApplePayPaymentDataDto.description:
The encrypted payment payload. WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.ApplePayPaymentDataDto.Data is the base64-encoded
AES-GCM ciphertext that decrypts to the card credentials; WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.ApplePayPaymentDataDto.Signature
is the CMS signature that proves the payload came from Apple. Both are sensitive
and MUST NOT be logged.

ApplePayPaymentHeaderDto.description:
Header carried alongside the encrypted payload. WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.ApplePayPaymentHeaderDto.EphemeralPublicKey
is the ECDH ephemeral key used during decryption and must not be logged.

ApplePayPaymentMethodDto.description:
Wallet-side display metadata for the chosen card on the Apple Pay sheet. None
of these fields carry PAN/CVV — they are safe-to-log presentation values.

ApplePayProcessPaymentOutput.description:
Response shape for the stub process-payment endpoint. Mirrors the POC return
value (`{ success: true }`). Carries no decrypted card data.

currentBatchIds.description:
Per-processor open batch IDs for this merchant, keyed by lower-cased processor key
(e.g. `"tsys"`, `"loopback"`). Transactions authorized for a given processor
while its batch is open are stamped with that processor's ID. When settlement starts,
only the rotating processor's entry is rotated to a new value — sibling processors'
boundaries are unaffected. Empty until the first settlement run or first transaction
that needs batch assignment.
Format: `{merchantId-short}:{date}:{sequence}`.

currentBatchId.description:
Legacy single-scalar batch ID (the original shape, pre per-processor migration).
Read-compat only — the
`BatchIdManager` (in `PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Domain`) falls back to this
when Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.Autosettle.AutosettlementSettings.CurrentBatchIds has no
entry for the requested processor, treating it as that processor's open batch. The first
successful rotation under the new code populates Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.Autosettle.AutosettlementSettings.CurrentBatchIds for that
processor and clears this scalar. New writes never set this field.

CardVerificationSettings.description:
Per-merchant accept-list of AVS and CVV response codes. A flag set to `true`
means transactions returning that code are accepted; `false` means they are
rejected post-authorization. US AVS codes and every CVV code default to
`true`, so a brand-new merchant accepts every domestic response out of the
box. The eight international AVS codes (B, C, D, F, G, I, M, P: the same set
canonicalised by `CardVerificationSettingsValidator.InternationalAvsCodes`)
default to `false`, so a freshly-onboarded merchant rejects international
responses until it explicitly opts in.

Cardholder physically present at the point of sale (retail/in-store flow).
Mail-order / telephone-order — cardholder not present and the merchant captured the account number through a non-electronic channel (fax, phone, paper form).
E-commerce — cardholder not present and the transaction was originated through a website, mobile application, or other electronic channel.
Recurring / subscription — cardholder is not contemporaneously present; the merchant is charging a stored credential against a prior cardholder authorization.

ClientIpGeoSnapshot.description: Point-in-time snapshot of geolocation and ISP/ASN data resolved from the transaction's Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.ClientIpAddress at the enrichment stage of the orchestration pipeline. This snapshot is immutable after creation. Subsequent updates to the transaction (capture, refund, reversal, repeat, recurring-billing materializations) MUST NOT overwrite it — the snapshot captures the geo intelligence as it was at the moment the original transaction ran. If the underlying IP intelligence database changes (DB-IP MMDB upgrade, ASN reassignment, ISP rebrand, etc.) the persisted snapshot is preserved so historical transactions remain auditable against the data the system saw at runtime. All fields are nullable because not every IP record carries every column — fine-grained fields like Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.ClientIpGeoSnapshot.City are sparse for IP ranges that DB-IP can only localize to a country or region.

legacyNumber.description:
The contract's legacy numeric key, as used by the v1 API where contracts are identified by an
integer rather than a Guid. Server-owned: stamped once at create from a tenant-scoped counter
and never settable from an inbound payload.

creationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was created.

creatorId.description: The ID of the user who created this entity.

lastModificationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was last modified.

lastModifierId.description: The ID of the user who last modified this entity.

isDeleted.description: Indicates whether this entity has been deleted.

deleterId.description: The ID of the user who deleted this entity, if it is deleted.

deletionTime.description: The date and time when this entity was deleted, if it is deleted.

concurrencyStamp.description:
Optimistic-concurrency stamp for the embedded contract. Contracts live inside
the Customer aggregate document, so they carry no per-contract Cosmos ETag; this stamp lets
the Contract API enforce per-contract optimistic concurrency independently of the parent
document. Nullable because documents created before this field carry no stamp: a null stamp
means "no concurrency check" until the contract is next updated, which stamps it going forward.

consecutiveFailures.description:
Consecutive failed billing attempts without an intervening success. Reset to 0 on success.
Used with Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.MaxFailCount to determine suspension.

lastSuccessfulExecution.description: Timestamp of the last successful billing execution.

lastExecution.description: Timestamp of the last billing execution (success or failure).

executionHistory.description:
The most recent execution records for this contract (capped at 10, newest first).
Default-initialized to an empty list so new contract documents persist an empty
`"ExecutionHistory": []` in Cosmos — EF Core Cosmos cannot reliably add
detached owned-collection items to a property whose loaded JObject path does
not contain the key (throws System.NullReferenceException in
`DocumentSource.GetCurrentDocument` during `SaveChangesAsync`).


Remains nullable because Newtonsoft deserialization overrides the C# initializer
when the persisted document has an explicit `"ExecutionHistory": null`
(legacy contracts predating this default-initialization fix). Callers must
normalize to an empty list before mutating (`ExecutionHistory ??= []`)
until those docs are backfilled.

Describes why a recurring billing contract was deactivated.
Persisted on the contract document for diagnostics and reporting.

Total execution count (successful + failed) reached MaxNumPayments.
Successful execution count reached MaxSuccessfulBills.
Cumulative amount billed reached MaxAmount.
The recurrence schedule produced no further occurrences — either the Until end date was reached or the recurrence count was exhausted.
Manually deactivated by an operator via the UI or API.

ContractDto.description:
Data transfer object representing a recurring billing contract, including execution statistics,
schedule configuration, and payment method details.

executedAt.description: The date and time the billing execution was performed.

success.description: Whether the billing attempt was approved by the payment processor.

amountBilled.description: The amount charged in this billing execution.

transactionId.description: The transaction ID created in the payment engine, if one was created.

failureReason.description: An explanation of why the billing execution failed. Null for successful attempts.

responseCode.description:
The processor response code for this execution. Used for failure classification
against Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.FailureRetryResultCodes.

scheduledRunTime.description:
The scheduled occurrence time this execution was triggered for.
Used by the Layer 2 idempotency guard to detect duplicate billing for the same
scheduled occurrence. Null for execution records created before this field was added.

ContractExecutionRecord.description:
A single execution record for a recurring billing contract, capturing the outcome
of one billing attempt. Stored as part of Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractAggregates.ExecutionHistory
(capped at the most recent 10 entries).

paymentTokenId.description: Internal vault identifier of a previously stored payment method, valid for both Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card and Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check contracts. This value correlates directly to stored cardholder data and is an internal binding: prefer Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.PaymentTokenReference on every external integration. It remains accepted inbound for callers that have not yet migrated, and is resolved and re-stamped server-side on every contract write.

paymentTokenReference.description: The externally-emitted, chargeable public reference of the stored payment method this contract bills: the opaque `pt_`-prefixed handle returned when the payment method was stored. This is the identifier external integrations should use, and it is valid for both Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card and Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check contracts.

ContractPayMethod.description: Represents a payment method attached to a recurring billing contract. Exactly one of two shapes is expected on a Create request: Tokenised: set Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.PaymentTokenReference (the opaque `pt_` handle) to reference a previously stored payment method, for either Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type = Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card or Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type = Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check. Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Card and Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Check must be left null; the recurring billing engine resolves the underlying card or bank-account data from the token store at execution time. This is the recommended shape because it keeps PCI scope at the token layer.Raw: populate Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Card (when Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type is Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card) or Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Check (when Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type is Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check) with the account data. Both token fields must be null. The Create validator rejects payloads that mix both shapes (a token alongside raw Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Card/Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Check data) or that omit both.

ContractPayMethodType.description: Specifies the available payment method types that can be associated with a contract.

count.description: The number of occurrences in a particular recurrence.

until.description: The datetime that bounds the current recurrence.

nextScheduledRun.description:
The next computed billing date. Persisted after each billing run to avoid
re-expanding the full recurrence series every cycle. Enables efficient Cosmos queries
(filter at DB level: `contract.Schedule.NextScheduledRun <= now`).
Null for contracts that have never been scheduled or have ended.

startDate.description:
The earliest date on which this contract is eligible to bill. Set by the user
when creating the contract (defaults to the creation date) and may be set to a
future date to delay first billing. The recurrence engine anchors expansion to
this date and the daily billing job will not fire a contract whose
Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.Recurrence.ContractSchedule.StartDate is in the future.
            
Null on legacy documents that predate this field. The canonical fallback chain
callers MUST use is `StartDate ?? Contract.CreationTime ?? DateTime.UtcNow`,
applied server-side by `ContractCrudAppService.ResolveScheduleAnchor`.
The UI does not expand the recurrence for a saved contract at all: it reads
Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.Recurrence.ContractSchedule.NextScheduledRun through `ContractNextRunCalculator`, and only
previews an unsaved schedule (anchored on this date, or now when it has none).

maxAmount.description:
Total amount the contract may bill across its lifetime before it deactivates itself.
Leave it empty for no limit. The contract create and update endpoints require a value
greater than zero when one is supplied; a non-positive value stored by an older save is
read as no limit.

maxNumPayments.description:
Total number of billing attempts, successful or not, the contract may make before it
deactivates itself. Leave it empty for no limit. The contract create and update endpoints
require at least 1 when a value is supplied; a non-positive value stored by an older save
is read as no limit.

maxSuccessfulBills.description:
Number of successful bills the contract may take before it deactivates itself. Leave it
empty for no limit. The contract create and update endpoints require at least 1 when a
value is supplied; a non-positive value stored by an older save is read as no limit.

maxFailCount.description:
Consecutive failed billing attempts that suspend the contract. Empty or `0` means the
contract is never suspended for failures and retries indefinitely. Unlike the three
capacity caps above, `0` is a valid, accepted value here.

failureInterval.description:
How many Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.FailurePeriod units to wait before retrying after a failed billing
attempt. Applied together with Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.FailurePeriod.

failureRetryResultCodes.description:
Processor response codes that count toward the Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.MaxFailCount suspension threshold.
If a failure's response code is NOT in this list, the failure retries indefinitely
until the contract ends. If the code IS in this list and consecutive failures reach
Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.MaxFailCount, the contract is suspended.
Null or empty means all failure codes count toward suspension.

A percentage of the transaction base amount. Permitted only under the card-brand Government / Higher-Education service-fee program, and therefore gated behind the merchant Government/Education attestation. The per-network applicability guard (block on Visa, allow where the network permits) is enforced separately at transaction time.

ConvenienceFeePaymentChannel.description: A payment channel a merchant operates, used to justify a general-program convenience fee (epic #3157, channel-model story #3207). The card brands permit a convenience fee only when it is charged on a genuine alternative channel and a distinct standard channel also exists for the cardholder — the fee is for the channel, not for the card type.
x-enumDescriptions: Face-to-face, cardholder physically present. A standard channel; never an alternative.
Mail order (the cardholder mails payment). A standard channel; never an alternative.
Payment by check. A standard channel; never an alternative.
Online / e-commerce. A qualifying alternative channel; never a standard channel.
Telephone order. Valid as either a standard channel or a qualifying alternative channel.
Self-service kiosk / unattended terminal. A qualifying alternative channel only — not "in person" per the card-brand FAQ. Never a standard channel.

hostedPageId.description: The HPP configuration ID this session targets. Required.

customerId.description:
Optional trusted customer id the merchant binds to this session. When supplied, the
session relates to exactly this one customer: customer resolution at consent-capture
time uses this id exclusively and never falls back to the ambiguous cardholder-email
find-or-create, and the resulting transaction's `InvoiceData.CustomerId` is stamped
from it server-side. The id is validated at session-create time to exist, be active, and
belong to the session's merchant; a missing, inactive/soft-deleted, or cross-merchant id
is rejected. `null` (the default) preserves the historical anonymous behavior where
the customer is found-or-created from the cardholder email collected on the form.

prefilledFields.description:
Pre-populated field key/value pairs used to pre-fill the payment form. Use one of the well-known
field keys listed below, or an enabled merchant custom field name. Keys reserved for sensitive card
data or internal identifiers are always rejected.


Handling of an unrecognized custom-field key depends on whether the target page scopes its custom
fields (see the hosted page's custom-field allow-list). When the page does NOT scope its custom
fields, an unrecognized key is accepted but ignored when the form is rendered (unchanged behavior).
When the page DOES scope its custom fields, a key that is not a well-known field and not one of the
page's allowed custom fields is rejected at session create with an error naming the offending key.
Conditional: When SaveCardOnly is true.
Conditional: When AmountMode == Suggested.
Conditional: When PrefilledFields > 0.

Valid keys (in addition to enabled merchant custom field names):

- `allowed_payment_methods`: Comma-separated list of payment-method keys the session permits (e.g. card,ach).
            A directive, not a form field: it narrows the page's rendered payment methods for this
            session (intersection with the page's configured + capability-filtered methods). Empty
            or absent means no session-level restriction. Values must be recognized
            payment-method keys; session creation rejects unrecognized entries
- `base_amount`: Base transaction amount
- `billing_address1`: Billing address line 1
- `billing_address2`: Billing address line 2
- `billing_city`: Billing city
- `billing_country`: Billing country
- `billing_first_name`: Billing first name
- `billing_last_name`: Billing last name
- `billing_phone`: Billing phone number
- `billing_state`: Billing state or province
- `billing_zip`: Billing ZIP or postal code
- `convenience_fee`: Convenience fee amount
- `customer_email`: Customer email address
- `invoice_number`: Invoice number
- `order_summary`: JSON-serialized order summary containing line items and totals.
            Used to render a detailed summary panel on the payment page.
            Value must be a valid  JSON string
- `shipping`: Shipping amount
- `shipping_address1`: Shipping address line 1
- `shipping_address2`: Shipping address line 2
- `shipping_city`: Shipping city
- `shipping_country`: Shipping country
- `shipping_first_name`: Shipping first name
- `shipping_last_name`: Shipping last name
- `shipping_phone`: Shipping phone number
- `shipping_state`: Shipping state or province
- `shipping_zip`: Shipping ZIP or postal code
- `suppress_convenience_fee`: Declares that this session authoritatively carries no convenience fee, so the public
            surfaces must neither seed one from the merchant's convenience-fee configuration nor recompute
            a percentage one, and must render no fee line and no disclosure block. A directive, not a form
            field: it states a producer's decision rather than a value the payer sees. Must be one of the
             values (true, false); session
            creation rejects anything else. Absent means no declaration, which is the pre-directive
            behaviour: the surfaces resolve the fee themselves
- `surcharge`: Surcharge amount
- `tax`: Tax amount
- `tip`: Tip amount
- `vault_restriction`: Vault-restriction directive controlling how the payment instrument may be stored for
            this session. Must be one of the  constants
            (any, allow_new_and_saved, saved_only). A directive, not a form
            field. Absent means no restriction (any)

requireConsent.description:
Optional per-session override for whether ticking the stored-credential consent box is
mandatory before the payment can be submitted. `null` (the default) inherits the
tenant-level `StoredCredentialConsents.RequireConsent` setting, preserving historical
behavior. `true` forces consent to be required for this session (the cardholder must
tick the box to pay); `false` makes it optional (the box is still shown, but the
cardholder may submit a normal sale without ticking it — no token is vaulted and no consent
record is written when they decline).

tokenizeOnPayment.description:
Optional — declares whether the cardholder's card should be vaulted as a reusable
`PaymentToken` when this session's payment succeeds. `null` (the default) defers
to the merchant's `MerchantFeatureSettings.HppTokenizeOnPaymentDefault` flag;
`true` forces tokenization on for this session; `false` forces it off regardless
of the merchant default.

saveCardOnly.description: Optional — when `true`, this session saves the cardholder's card without charging it: the gateway runs a zero-dollar account verification (authorize $0 + AVS/CVV, immediate void) instead of a payment, then vaults the card and captures consent. Used for "save card now, charge later" onboarding / add-card-to-wallet. Default `false` (a normal chargeable session).

parentOrigin.description:
Optional HTTPS origin (scheme + host, e.g. `https://shop.example.com`) of the parent
page that will embed this HPP session in an iframe. When set, the HPP page emits
`postMessage` lifecycle events (`ready`, `session_loaded`,
`payment_succeeded`, etc.) using this value as the `targetOrigin`; never `'*'`.
The host portion must match an entry in the resolved page's `AllowedEmbeddingDomains`
(wildcard subdomains supported). When `null`, postMessage emission is disabled
(fail-closed) and the iframe still works for non-embedded use.
Conditional: When ParentOrigin is not empty. Max length: 2048.

enableFieldEvents.description: Optional opt-in to per-field `field_focused` / `field_blurred` postMessage events. When `true`, the iframe attaches a single delegated focus/blur listener on the form root and emits one envelope per focus boundary with the element's `data-hpp-field` identifier. Field values are NEVER included. When `false` (the default) no listener is registered, so there is no JS boundary at which a value could leak. Requires PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.CreateHppSessionInput.ParentOrigin to be set — otherwise the emitter is fail-closed and emits nothing regardless of this flag.

this (the JS client calls `onvalidatemerchant` → our backend POSTs to
Apple's `startSession`). Wallets that don't issue server-side sessions
(Google Pay) won't implement
!:WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.Providers.IWalletPaymentSessionProvider
and the orchestrator returns "operation not supported by this provider".
            


The caller (HPP browser) supplies only the merchant being checked out on plus
the chosen provider type. Server-side resolution determines which persisted
`WalletProviderRegistration` row applies, using the merchant's own
`DigitalWallets[]` bindings — the Level / Platform-vs-Merchant
distinction is an internal data-modeling concept and never crosses the wire.

stored payment methods, and associated recurring billing contracts.

customName.description:
Optional user-defined name for this stored payment method (e.g., "Marriott Chase",
"Bank of America Checkcard"). When set, takes priority over the computed display name.
Nullable for Cosmos backward compatibility — existing documents won't have this field.

initialSchemeTransactionId.description:
The initial (first-in-series) network / scheme transaction id captured from the processor's
authorization response on the cardholder-initiated credential-on-file transaction that stored
this credential. Lets any later transaction (CIT-COF or MIT, any card brand) resolve and echo
the original network transaction id from just the stored token / payment method, without
depending on a StoredCredentialConsent lookup.

lastSchemeTransactionId.description:
The most-recent-in-series network / scheme transaction id. At tokenization this equals
Phoenix.SharedModels.Customer.CustomerStoredPaymentMethod.InitialSchemeTransactionId. Card-network rules (Visa 11.1.5, Mastercard 13.1.1)
allow the most recent value in a series to be sent when the original is unavailable, so a later
story can advance this on each subsequent authorization response without losing the first-in-
series anchor. Nullable / non-sensitive as for Phoenix.SharedModels.Customer.CustomerStoredPaymentMethod.InitialSchemeTransactionId.

schemeTransactionIdBrand.description:
The card brand at the moment the network transaction id was captured (e.g. "Visa",
"Mastercard", "Discover", "Amex"). Retained because a co-branded card can switch networks
after storage; Mastercard's AltNetTranID handling requires the brand-at-capture to detect the
case where a stored Visa id must be sent in a Mastercard field. Emitting AltNetTranID is out of
scope here — this only preserves the data so the downstream echo work is not precluded.
Nullable / non-sensitive.

schemeTransactionIdProcessor.description:
The processor the network transaction id originated from ("tsys" / "fiserv"). The two
processors' response formats differ (TSYS a single 15-char Transaction Identifier; Fiserv
per-brand, whose Visa value can exceed 15 chars including the trailing Validation Code), so the
id is stored opaquely and tagged with its originating processor. Nullable / non-sensitive.

publicReference.description:
The externally-emitted, chargeable `PublicReference` of the backing `PaymentToken`
(the opaque `pt_`-prefixed handle) captured when this stored method was minted. Persisted
here so the tokenize-on-payment path can surface it on the transaction response / webhook
without re-reading the token, and so a later charge can round-trip the merchant-facing handle.
Distinct from Phoenix.SharedModels.Customer.CustomerStoredPaymentMethod.PaymentTokenId, which is the internal vault Guid (PAN-correlated,
never emitted). Nullable for Cosmos backward compatibility: stored methods minted before this
field predate it and carry `null` until the one-time DbMigrator backfill
(`CustomerStoredPaymentMethodPublicReferenceBackfillSeedContributor`) copies the backing
token's handle onto them. The backfill only ever fills a null and never rewrites an assigned
handle. Non-sensitive (an opaque random handle, not a PAN).

readerTokenFingerprint.description:
Dedupe fingerprint for a reader-token-backed (PAN-less) stored method: a one-way SHA-256
digest of the processor reader token that this method's backing vault token carries. Set
only for the reader-token shape (decrypt-and-forward processors such as MagTek DAF, where
the gateway never sees the PAN); `null` for every PAN- or account-backed method.

digest of the routing number combined with the account number's last four digits. Set only
for the Check shape; `null` for card and reader-token methods.

DestinationSuppressionReason.description:

app restart, mirroring a SendGrid-style suppression list.
x-enumDescriptions: The endpoint failed the configured number of sustained consecutive delivery attempts.

The endpoint returned a permanent (non-retryable) HTTP client error (a 4xx other than 401 / 403 / 408 / 429), signalling the request is wrong-by-construction (URL gone, payload refused) and will keep failing the same way on retry.
An administrator suppressed the endpoint manually.

The endpoint repeatedly rejected our credentials (401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden). Kept distinct from PermanentHttpError so an operator can tell an auth-plane problem (expired secret, WAF rule, IP allowlist) from an endpoint that is genuinely gone: the two call for completely different remediation. value.description:
The value the rule compares against, coerced to the target column's type when the predicate is
built. Declared `object?` so one rule shape serves every column type.

Phoenix.Abp.Core.Data.Filtering.FilterValueJsonConverter normalizes this to a CLR primitive while reading JSON.
Without it, System.Text.Json boxes a `JsonElement` here for every HTTP caller, and each
consumer downstream (the Cosmos expression builder, the Transactions virtual-field rewriters)
silently dropped the rule.

caseInsensitive.description:
When true, string comparison operators (Equals, StartsWith, Contains, EndsWith)
apply `ToLower()` to both property and value before comparing.
Cosmos DB string comparisons are case-sensitive by default; this translates
to the `LOWER()` SQL function which is indexable.

forceCardNotPresent.description:
Force the network request to card-not-present routing even when the request data implies a
card-present capture (UMF POS entry / condition → CNP). Parity with the TSYS
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TsysCertificationOverrides.ForceCardNotPresent knob.

forceManualEntryMode.description:
Force the UMF POS entry mode to manual even when the captured entry mode is something else.
Parity with the TSYS Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TsysCertificationOverrides.ForceManualEntryMode knob.

merchantInitiatedReferenceOverride.description:
Hard-coded scheme / original-transaction id supplied to a Visa/MC MIT cert request when the
test merchant has no real prior CIT to reference.

merchantCategoryCodeOverride.description:
Transaction-level Merchant Category Code for a cert scenario. Production MCC is
merchant-config-only (`Merchant.Mcc`); this override lets the cert harness exercise an
MCC the configured merchant value does not carry.

billPaymentIndicatorOverride.description:
Force the Fiserv bill-payment indicator (`BillPayGrp.BillPymtTxnInd`) for a cert
scenario. Production maps the legacy bill-payment indicator to MIT semantics; this override
drives the raw UMF value directly.

forceLevel3WithSwipeEntry.description:
Emit Level 3 fields even when the captured entry mode is a magnetic-stripe swipe. Parity with
the TSYS Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TsysCertificationOverrides.ForceLevel3WithSwipeEntry knob; include only
if the Fiserv L3 cert suite requires L3 on swipe entry.

forcePinCapableTerminal.description:
Force the UMF terminal-capability fields to the PIN-capable card-present shape the certified
RPH012 baseline claims: `POSEntryMode` third digit `1` (keyed `011` / swiped
`901`), `TermEntryCapablt``01`, and `CardCaptCap``1`. Production
terminals never claim PIN capability today (see `ProcessorHandlerFiserv.BuildCommonGrp`),
so this is a cert-only escape hatch until a real merchant/terminal-profile setting drives these
fields for production traffic (tracked as a follow-up story).

$processor.description: Type discriminator identifying these overrides as the fiserv shape. Must be sent as "fiserv".

FiservCertificationOverrides.description:
Fiserv-specific certification override knobs. Drive the Fiserv Rapid Connect (UMF) outbound
message at auth/settle time when the cert harness needs to exercise a path the
production-shape request fields cannot otherwise reach.

query.

HppCaptureMode.description:
Capture timing for a chargeable Hosted Payment Page (the "Payment" flow). This is an axis
orthogonal to card storage: a page composes a capture mode with the existing save-card option
(tokenization / `SavePaymentDetails`) rather than encoding the combination as a dedicated
Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose value. "Save card + delayed capture" is therefore simply
Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.Payment + Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppCaptureMode.Authorize + save-card enabled.
x-enumDescriptions: Authorize and capture funds in a single step (the historical, default behavior). null resolves here, so every pre-existing chargeable page keeps doing an implicit Sale.

Authorize now, capture later (delayed capture). The resulting transaction is an Authorization in an Authorized state, eligible for capture and void per the action matrix; the capture is completed later against the resulting transaction id via the existing capture action path (including the Apple Pay single-use token case).

HppPagePurpose.description:
First-class, instance-level classification of what a hosted payment page is for. Lets a
merchant dedicate a specific HPP instance to a non-payment task (collecting and storing card
details) instead of flipping a per-session flag on every link.
x-enumDescriptions: The default, historical behavior: a chargeable payment page. null resolves here, so every pre-existing HPP instance keeps behaving exactly as before.

A card-capture page: the cardholder's card is validated via a zero-dollar account verification (authorize $0 + AVS/CVV, immediate void), then vaulted with stored-credential consent. No charge is taken. Amount-bearing configuration (tax, shipping, convenience fee, invoice amounts, donations, tip) is irrelevant and is hidden in the builder / rejected by the validator. Requires the merchant's processor to advertise SupportsZeroDollarVerification.

A card-capture page that also charges the first of a recurring schedule. The cardholder's card is charged a real initial sale (the first payment of a referenced reusable recurring plan, framed as the customer-initiated transaction that establishes the credential-on-file agreement), vaulted with Recurring stored-credential consent, and a customer Contract is created for the remaining payments. Like SaveCard, the amount-bearing builder configuration (tax, shipping, convenience, invoice, donations, tip, customer-set amount) is hidden: the charged amount is driven entirely by the inlined recurring definition, not by per-page amount fields. Requires a complete inlined recurring definition (RecurringPlan).

cardholder navigates to, or as a chrome-less surface mounted inside a merchant-site iframe.
This governs page chrome only (outer surface background, full-viewport height, page padding).
It never changes the session flow, the fields collected, or any compliance content: consent
capture, the NACHA WEB authorization, the convenience-fee disclosure, and the confirmation
panel render identically in both modes.
x-enumDescriptions: The default, historical behavior: a full standalone page with the surface background, full-viewport minimum height, and the standard outer page padding. null (legacy sessions) resolves here.

A chrome-less compact presentation for mounting inside a merchant-site iframe: no standalone page surface or full-viewport height, tight paddings, and narrow-width behavior that stays readable down to a 320 px viewport without horizontal scrolling.

the page's own amount configuration: when a session declares a mode other than

Whether the cardholder's payment method will be vaulted as a reusable token. This is the
effective decision after the merchant's tokenize-by-default setting is applied and after the
targeted page's tokenization toggle (`SupportTokenization` / `SavePaymentDetails`)
has had its say. A request that asked for `tokenizeOnPayment: true` against a page whose
merchant disabled tokenization reports `false` here: that is the veto, which previously
only appeared in a server-side log line. Always `true` for a card-capture purpose, which
exists to store the credential.

Whether this session stores the payment method with no charge at all. `true` for a
resolved Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.SaveCard purpose or an explicit `saveCardOnly`
request on a Payment page. Deliberately `false` for
Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.SaveCardWithInitialCharge, which takes a real initial charge, so
a request that sent `saveCardOnly: true` against that purpose reports `false` here.

The customer this session is bound to, echoed from the request's `customerId` after it

The prefilled field keys stored on the session, in no particular order. Values are never

server may add one: deriving a locked amount from a fixed-amount page stamps
`base_amount` even when the request supplied none.

ignoredPrefillKeys.description:
The subset of PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HppSessionEffectiveShapeDto.PrefilledFieldKeys that the hosted page will silently ignore
when it renders: keys that are neither a well-known field nor an enabled, page-visible
merchant custom field. They are accepted and persisted rather than rejected, for backward
compatibility, so this list is the only signal that a key will have no effect (usually a
typo, or a custom field that is disabled or hidden for hosted pages).

HppSessionPurpose.description:
Classifies the calling context that produced an HPP session, which in turn drives the
allowed TTL bounds and any other purpose-specific policy. The default is
PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HppSessionPurpose.CheckoutLink, which is the historical merchant-facing pay-link behavior
with a 1-minute–15-minute TTL ceiling appropriate for hot checkout flows.
x-enumDescriptions: Standard merchant-facing pay-link session. Short TTL (60s–900s).
Session created by the invoicing module's send flow to back an invoice's pay-link. Long TTL (1h–90d) so the link survives net-30 invoice terms with margin for late payment.

Session created by the Merchant Billing module to back a stored-payment-method capture link emailed to a merchant. Long TTL (1h–90d) so a link sent now can be completed days later, on the merchant's own time, rather than synchronously by an operator.

HppSessionStatus.description:
Represents the lifecycle status of an HPP session.
Expired is not a stored status — sessions are removed by Cosmos TTL.
x-enumDescriptions: The session has been created and is awaiting use by a customer. Also the status a session returns to when a premature consume is released: a submission that was rejected by pure request-shape validation before the orchestrator was invoked leaves the link usable, so the payer can correct their input and resubmit on the same link (see Consumed).

The session has been consumed by a transaction submission. Terminal in practice: the only exit is the narrow release back to Pending performed by HppSession.ReleaseConsume, which requires that the session carries no OrchestratorDispatchedAt marker, that the consuming transaction id is still the one recorded, and that no vault token was minted. Once a submission reaches the orchestrator the marker is durable and the session stays Consumed regardless of the outcome, including a decline. Submit paths additionally validate the request BEFORE consuming, so a rejected request usually never spends the link in the first place; the release covers the rules that can only run inside the create.
The session has been manually revoked by an administrator.

The session was cancelled by the parent page via the iframe two-way command channel Distinct from Revoked (admin-initiated) for clarity in audit + reporting — same terminal effect (session can no longer be consumed).

incrementalAmount.description:
The additional authorization amount to request, in major currency units (e.g. `10.00`
= $10). The new `Total_Auth_Amt` after a successful incremental auth equals the
existing approved amount plus this value. Must be strictly positive — clearing or
reducing an existing hold is the reversal flow's job, not this one.

Surfaced on the close-stage history entry and the customer-facing receipt. Not validated
against any controlled vocabulary — purely informational.

isEmpty.description:
true when the bundle carries no actionable information. An
            incremental authorization with a non-positive increment has nothing to ask the
            brand for and is a caller error — the AppService precondition rejects this shape
            before any orchestration round-trip is dispatched.

IncrementalAuthorizationFields.description:
Structured field bundle for the
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionOperationType.IncrementalAuthorization
operation. An incremental authorization sends a fresh auth message to the
brand network on top of the existing approved hold, increasing the held amount by the
requested increment. The issuer can decline.

InitiationType.description:
Identifies who initiated a payment transaction. Required for PCI-compliant stored credential handling
and for correctly flagging transactions to card networks (CIT vs MIT indicators).
x-enumDescriptions: The cardholder is present or otherwise authorizing this specific charge contemporaneously. Default for transactions originated by the cardholder through HPP checkout, API with cardholder interaction, or virtual terminal sales with the cardholder present.

The merchant is initiating this charge without contemporaneous cardholder authorization, relying on prior consent captured on an earlier cardholder-initiated transaction. Used for recurring billing, unscheduled credential-on-file charges, resubmissions, and other merchant-triggered uses of a stored credential.

MerchantBillingCaptureLinkStatus.description:
Operator-visible status of the outstanding send-a-link capture link for a billed merchant's
stored payment method. Derived from the latest link-origin
`MerchantBillingPaymentMethodCaptureIntent` for the (reseller, merchant) pair; the intent is
the source of truth (its consumed / cancelled / expiry markers map one-to-one to these states).
x-enumDescriptions: No capture link has been sent for this merchant (no link-origin intent exists).
A link has been sent and is still usable: issued, not yet consumed, not cancelled, and not past its expiry. The merchant can complete the hosted page; the operator can resend or cancel it.
The merchant completed the hosted page: the bound capture-intent was consumed.
The link passed its expiry without being consumed or cancelled. It can be reissued.
An operator revoked the link before it was used. Its hosted page can no longer be completed; it can be reissued.

expiresAt.description: When the link (and its bound session/intent) expires, in UTC. Null when no link exists.

canResend.description:
Whether a resend action is available: true whenever a link exists (a usable link is resent for
its existing session; an expired/cancelled/completed one is reissued fresh).

canCancel.description: Whether a cancel action is available: only a still-usable (pending) link can be revoked.

PII, or any card/account detail.

MerchantBillingRunBatchStatus.description:
Status of an admin all-resellers billing fan-out batch. A batch wraps the
per-reseller PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunStatus runs the Durable fan-out workflow
produces; only one non-terminal (PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunBatchStatus.Pending/PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunBatchStatus.Running) batch may be
in flight at a time (the batch-level single-in-flight guard).
x-enumDescriptions: Batch created and the workflow has been started but discovery has not run yet.
The fan-out workflow is running per-reseller billing runs.
Every reseller that ran completed without a failed reseller run.
At least one reseller ran successfully and at least one reseller run failed.
No reseller ran successfully and at least one reseller run failed.

An admin force-cleared the batch from the Billing Runs page. A terminal, non-failure state distinct from Failed: it records a deliberate operator action (releasing a stuck or stale batch) rather than a run that errored. Like every other terminal status it is reclaimable by the next fan-out's lock-recovery, and is never treated as in-progress.

MerchantBillingRunResultStatus.description: Outcome status for an individual merchant within a billing run.
x-enumDescriptions: Merchant rated successfully. Terminal for a dry run; on a non-dry run it is a transient pre-dispatch state that the fulfillment dispatcher advances to a path-specific status (Invoiced or ChargePending).
Billing failed for this merchant.
Merchant was skipped (e.g., inactive or excluded).
No active price plan assigned to this merchant.
No usage recorded for this merchant in the billing period.

Neither ResellerBillingPreferences.DefaultFulfillmentPath nor the per-merchant MerchantBillingAssignment.FulfillmentPath override is set, so the resolver cannot decide how to collect payment for this merchant.
The effective fulfillment path is RecurringContract but no active MerchantBillingPaymentMethod row exists for the (ResellerId, MerchantId) pair, so the recurring charge has no token to draft against.
The effective fulfillment path is RecurringContract but the reseller has not configured a CollectionMerchantId, so there is no party to own the recurring contract.
The effective fulfillment path is Invoicing but the reseller has not configured an HppPageId, so the generated invoice has no payment link destination.
The merchant was rated successfully and the Invoicing fulfillment path produced an issued invoice. Terminal for the Invoicing path — see MerchantBillingRunResult.InvoiceId for the artifact.

The RecurringContract path charge completed successfully. Set when the downstream charge reconciliation (tracked separately) confirms an approved transaction; see MerchantBillingRunResult.TransactionId.

The merchant was rated successfully and the RecurringContract path dispatched a charge request into the Transaction Manager. The charge has not yet been reconciled; the run records this as a non-terminal "awaiting result" state. See MerchantBillingRunResult.ContractId.
The RecurringContract path charge was attempted but declined or errored. Set by the downstream charge reconciliation (tracked separately).

Usage was recorded for the merchant in the billing period, but the plan produced no positive-charge line item, so there is nothing to bill. Distinct from NoUsage (which means no usage aggregates existed at all): here the merchant genuinely transacted, the usage simply fell entirely within a rate entry's included/free allowance or matched no billable rate entry. Where a rate entry matched the usage, the rated run keeps the zero-billable line item visible so the operator can see the usage and why it was not charged; usage that matched no rate entry produces no line item.

enablePaymentTokenization.description:

(Phoenix.SharedModels.Reseller.ResellerFeatures.PaymentTokenization). `null` means inherit the

`false` means do not tokenize by default; `true` opts the merchant's HPP
sessions into tokenize-on-payment unless a session overrides it. The targeted page must
still allow tokenization (Classic `SupportTokenization` / Streamlined
`SavePaymentDetails`) and a tokenizing session must declare a stored-credential
consent scope.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable identifier of the rule that produced the warning. For card-
verification surface warnings this is the property name on
`Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.CardVerificationSettings` (e.g. `"AvNoMatchIntl"`).

propertyName.description:
Dotted path to the field the warning applies to, suitable for UI field highlighting
(e.g. `"Processing.CardVerification.AvNoMatchIntl"`). May be empty when the
warning is not anchored to a single field.

message.description:
Human-readable message describing the condition for this specific warning. Should be
short and code-specific; shared rationale common to a group of warnings belongs in
PhoeniXGate.Merchants.MerchantSaveWarning.GroupRationale so renderers can emit it once per group.

groupRationale.description:
Optional explanation shared by every warning a rule produces. When present, renderers
MAY collapse warnings with an equal PhoeniXGate.Merchants.MerchantSaveWarning.GroupRationale into one shared
paragraph plus a flat list of PhoeniXGate.Merchants.MerchantSaveWarning.Code values, rather than repeating the
rationale inside every PhoeniXGate.Merchants.MerchantSaveWarning.Message. Null when the warning stands alone.

MerchantSaveWarning.description: Non-blocking informational warning attached to a merchant create/update response.

providerName.description:

fieldValues.description:
Values for the provider's configuration fields, keyed by field definition key. Values for fields

merchantId.description: The merchant the rollup belongs to.

merchantName.description:

(a merchant deleted after the transactions were taken, most commonly). The rollup is still
returned in that case so the amounts continue to reconcile.

transactionCount.description:
Number of approved transactions contributing to this rollup, counting both the sale side and
the credit side. Declined and in-flight transactions are excluded.

grossAmount.description:
Sum of the approved sale-side amounts (authorization, sale, force, capture, capture-all and
repeat sale) in the merchant's transaction currency.

netAmount.description:
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Reports.MerchantTransactionSummaryDto.GrossAmount less the approved credit-side amounts (returns and voids). This is
            the figure that reconciles against what the merchant is owed for the window.

transactionTypeCounts.description:
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Reports.MerchantTransactionSummaryDto.TransactionCount broken down by transaction type, keyed by the
            `TransactionType` member name (for example `Sale`, `Authorization`,
            `Return`, `Void`). Types with no activity in the window are omitted rather than
            carried as an explicit zero, so the keys present describe what the merchant actually did.
