tipAmount.description: Replacement gratuity in major currency units (e.g. `5.00` = $5.00). Mutates the settlement `` and `` elements and patches the transaction document's `/InvoiceData/Amounts/Tip` field when populated. `0` is interpreted as "clear the existing tip". The transaction's `Total` is intentionally not patched — `TrxAmounts.Total` is a computed property (`Base + Tip + Tax + Shipping + Convenience`) re-derived on every hydration, so the new tip flows through to the displayed Total automatically without a stored mutation. Wired today. Conditional: When TipAmount and HasValue meet conditions. Must be >= 0.

x-validation-rules.condition: When TipAmount and HasValue meet conditions

taxAmount.description: Replacement tax amount in major currency units. Settlement-only field — does not affect the transaction's running total. Used for interchange-rate qualification on the batch. Not yet implemented.

level3Amount.description: Replacement level-3 line-item subtotal in major currency units. Settlement-only field for level-3 (commercial card / GSA) interchange-rate qualification. Not yet implemented.

poNumber.description: Replacement purchase-order number. Settlement-only field for level-3 / level-2 commercial-card data. Not yet implemented.

billingStreet.description: Replacement AVS street value. Settlement-only field — used for retro AVS attachment when the original auth was processed without AVS. Not yet implemented.

billingZip.description: Replacement AVS postal/ZIP value. Settlement-only field — paired with PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Operations.OfflineAdjustmentFields.BillingStreet. Not yet implemented.

isEmpty.description:
true when no fields are populated. An empty bundle is a caller
            error — the OfflineAdjustment operation has nothing to apply.

isTipOnly.description:
true when only PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Operations.OfflineAdjustmentFields.TipAmount is populated (or no fields
            — but PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Operations.OfflineAdjustmentFields.IsEmpty would be checked first). Used by the contributor to
            short-circuit the non-tip wiring path that does not yet exist.

OfflineAdjustmentFields.description:
Structured field bundle for the OfflineAdjustment operation. Each property is optional;
only the populated fields are emitted into the adjustment-request XML and propagated
onto the corresponding transaction-document patches.
            
"Offline" denotes that the adjustment is applied to the transaction's settlement record
without contacting the processor network. Eligible fields are limited to those the
legacy `TipAdjustment.vb` path collected from `htData` (TIPAMT / TAXAMT /
LEVEL3AMT / PONUM / STREET / ZIP) — adjusting any other field requires re-authorization
at the rails (incremental authorization stage, separate ticket).
            
Industry eligibility for the tip-bearing path (TIPAMT) is enforced inside
`WinkPG.TransactionManager.ProcessorCommon.TipAdjustmentProcessor` today; lifting
the rule to a stage-level precondition is a deferred follow-up and is not duplicated
on this DTO.

dispositionSetAtUtc.description:
UTC timestamp of the moment Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PartialApprovalData.Disposition last moved. Set alongside every
disposition write, including the initial transition to
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PartialApprovalDisposition.Pending at detection time, so the age of a stuck
pending disposition is measurable.

dispositionDeadlineUtc.description:
UTC instant by which a Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PartialApprovalDisposition.Pending disposition must be
resolved before the gateway voids the reduced authorization on the operator's behalf.

requestedAmount.description:
The amount the gateway asked the issuer to authorize, in major currency units, snapshotted
at detection time. Kept here rather than read back from the response because a subsequent
reversal overwrites `/ResponseData`.

approvedAmount.description:
The lesser amount the issuer actually authorized, in major currency units, snapshotted at
detection time. The shortfall a split tender needs to collect is
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PartialApprovalData.RequestedAmount minus this value.

PartialApprovalData.description:
Durable record of a partial approval: the issuer authorized less than the requested amount,
and the gateway captured the evidence plus the lifecycle of the decision that followed.

PartialApprovalDisposition.description:
Tracks what happened to a partially approved authorization: the issuer approved less than
the requested amount, and someone (the operator, the cardholder, or a gateway timeout) has
to decide whether to keep the reduced authorization, void it, or collect the shortfall on a
second tender.
x-enumDescriptions: The partial approval has been detected and recorded, but nobody has decided its fate yet. The transaction is holding a reduced authorization at the issuer and is waiting on an operator/cardholder acknowledgment until DispositionDeadlineUtc elapses.
The reduced authorization was accepted as-is. No reversal is issued and the transaction proceeds through the normal capture/settlement path for the approved (lesser) amount.

The reduced authorization was rejected and reversed, so the issuer hold is released. The reason is recorded on VoidReason (operator choice, acknowledgment timeout, or an automatic gateway policy void).
The reduced authorization was kept and a follow-up tender was started to collect the shortfall. The continuation transaction carries the same SplitTenderGroupId with the next SplitTenderSequence.

PartialApprovalStrategy.description:
How the platform disposes of a partial approval: an authorization the issuer approved for less
than the requested amount, typically because the cardholder's available balance (or, for a
benefit card, the eligible balance) is lower than the sale.
x-enumDescriptions: Hold the partial authorization and wait for an operator to accept the approved amount or void it. The platform takes no action of its own until the operator answers, or until PartialApprovalAckTimeoutMinutes elapses.
Keep the approved amount without asking. The remainder is collected as a second tender when split tender is permitted, or left uncollected when it is not.
Void the partial authorization immediately and treat the sale as not completed. Use where a short payment is never acceptable and the cardholder should be asked for another card.

deniedCode.description:
The AVS or CVV response code that matched the denylist (e.g. "N", "P", "S").
This is a processor result code, not the cardholder's CVV input value.

deniedCodeType.description:
Whether the triggering code was an AVS or CVV result.
Expected values: `"Avs"` or `"Cvv"`.

deniedCodeDescription.description:
The logical key emitted by `CardVerificationFilter` identifying which
rule fired (e.g. `"AVNoMatch"`, `"CVNoMatch"`, `"AVZipOnly"`).
This is a stable, grep-friendly machine identifier — NOT a user-facing
sentence. The merchant detail page renders this value verbatim alongside
the human-readable rule label. If a future iteration wants prose
description text, add a separate property rather than overloading this
field. Safe to display to merchants — does not reveal the cardholder's
actual input.

ruleSource.description:
Identifies which denylist configuration rule triggered the rejection
(e.g., "AvsDeclineCodes", "CvvDeclineCodes", or a merchant-specific rule name).

rejectedAt.description: UTC timestamp of the denylist evaluation that triggered this rejection.

reversalResultMessage.description:
The result message from the reversal or void.
null if no reversal/void was attempted.

reversalAttemptedAt.description:
UTC timestamp of the reversal or void attempt.
null if no reversal/void was attempted.

requiresReversal.description:
Whether the orchestrator should schedule an auto-reversal for this policy
rejection. null (the default for historical gateway-side
rejections written before the field existed) is treated as "yes, reverse" —
the original behaviour. The native AVS/CVV decline path sets
false because the processor declined at auth time and never
placed a hold, so there is nothing to reverse and the
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PolicyRejectionData.ReversalResultCode / Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PolicyRejectionData.ReversalAttemptedAt fields
stay null.

PolicyRejectionData.description:
Records the post-authorization denylist match that caused a transaction to be policy-rejected.
Stored on the transaction so the merchant audit trail shows the full sequence:
auth approved → denylist matched → reversal/void issued → PolicyRejected.

billed against the requested price plan, ordered by merchant then period.

PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunResultStatus. An invoice settled after the run keeps
showing PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.BillingRuns.PricePlanHistoryPaymentStatus.Pending until charge reconciliation updates the run result.

fields are snapshots captured at run time (merchant name, plan name) so the report

PricingModel.description: Defines how the unit price for a product is determined.
x-enumDescriptions: A single fixed price per unit.
Price varies by quantity tier (e.g., 1-10 = $5, 11-50 = $4).
Price determined by metered usage (e.g., per GB, per API call).
Custom pricing negotiated per deal or contract.

Price manually overridden by the user.

Price from a negotiated contract or quote.

requireLevel2Data.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether card bins qualifying for level 2 processing are required
to supply level 2 data (manually or via order data defaults).

requireNameOnCard.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether the cardholder name must be provided
with the transaction regardless of entry mode.

requireZipCode.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether the billing zip code must be provided
with the transaction regardless of entry mode or AVS settings.

requireShipping.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the shipping amount must be provided with the transaction.

enableForceCapture.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether force capture transactions are allowed for this merchant.

requestProcessorToken.description:
Merchant preference for requesting a processor-issued reusable token at authorization
time, referenced elsewhere as `Processing.RequestProcessorToken`. Tri-state:
null (the default) means "auto", resolved ON wherever the routed
processor advertises processor tokenization; true / false
force the preference on or off. Surfaced on the merchant Processing tab as a tri-state
selector (Auto / Always request / Never request); carried on the DTO so the value
round-trips through the merchant create/update flow.

enableCreateIdempotency.description:
Opt-in for caller-facing create idempotency on the transaction-create surface, referenced
elsewhere as `Processing.EnableCreateIdempotency`. When true, a
caller-supplied `idempotencyKey` on a create is validated and claimed, so a retried
create returns the original transaction instead of charging again. null (the
default) and false both mean off: the key is accepted and persisted with no
validation and no dedup effect, exactly as it has always behaved.

processorProfiles.description:
Gets or sets the collection of processor profiles configured for this merchant.
Each profile maps a payment processor and its supported payment types.

screeningProviderProfiles.description:
Gets or sets the external screening providers configured for this merchant. Each profile points
at a registered screening provider and carries that provider's per-merchant field values.
Conditional: When ScreeningProviderProfiles is set.

registers.description: Gets or sets the collection of registers (point-of-sale terminals) assigned to this merchant.

ProcessingSettingsDto.description:
Data transfer object containing all processing-related settings for a merchant,
including duplicate checks, card verification, level 2/3 data requirements, processor profiles,
auto-settlement configuration, and register assignments.

$processor.description: Type discriminator naming the processor these certification overrides target. Required whenever processorCertificationOverrides is supplied. Accepted values: "fiserv", "tsys". Values are lower-case and case-sensitive.

ProcessorCertificationOverrides.description: Per-processor certification override knobs. These are cert-only escape hatches for forcing network-request indicators that production traffic never needs. Examples include flipping a card-present transaction to card-not-present routing for a specific cert scenario, or supplying a hard-coded scheme transaction id for a Visa MIT cert flow.

processorId.description:
Identifier of the processor this schema describes. Submit this as the processor configuration's
`ProcessorId` in a merchant create/update request.

fields.description:
The fields applicable to the requested payment types, ordered by
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.Position.

schemaVersion.description: Opaque, deterministic content hash of this processor's full projected field schema. It is derived from the field definitions (not hand-maintained), so it changes whenever a field is added, removed, or edited, and is stable otherwise. It is per-processor (covers the whole field catalog), so it does not vary with the `paymentTypes` filter. Cache the schema keyed by this value to detect drift; it is also returned as the response `ETag`, and a request with a matching `If-None-Match` receives `304 Not Modified`.

ProcessorConfigSchemaDto.description:
The configuration schema for a single processor: the set of fields a client must populate to
build a valid processor profile for that processor. Returned by the config-schema discovery
endpoint and intended to be paired with a merchant create/update request.

isValid.description:
True when every applicable field passed validation (no PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorConfigValidationResultDto.Results entry has
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldValidationResultDto.Ok == false).

results.description:
One entry per field that was evaluated for the requested payment-type selection. Fields outside
the selection are not evaluated and are omitted.

ProcessorConfigValidationResultDto.description:
Result of a stateless dry-run validation of a processor configuration payload. Returned by the
validate-config endpoint with HTTP 200 whether or not the payload is valid — it is a per-field
report, not an error response. No merchant document is written.

key.description:
Stable identifier used to store and retrieve the field value. Submit this verbatim as the
`Key` of the processor field value in a merchant create/update request.

name.description:
Human-friendly label for the field. Supplying it on the corresponding field value is optional;
when omitted, the server fills it from this definition.

description.description: Longer description or help text for the field.

options.description:
For dropdown fields, the selectable options as explicit `{value, label}` pairs. Submit
the option's `Value` verbatim as the field value. When a field has no distinct backing
wire code, `Value` equals `Label`. Null for non-dropdown fields. This is the
preferred shape for closed-set fields.

dropdownList.description:
For dropdown fields, the labels presented to the operator. Aligned by index with
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.DropdownValues when backing values differ from the labels.

dropdownValues.description:
For dropdown fields, the backing values stored for each option. When null, the label from
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.DropdownList is also the stored value.

isRequired.description: Whether a value must be supplied for this field, effective for the requested payment-type selection. When the config-schema request is scoped to a set of payment types, the response contains exactly the fields applicable to that selection and PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.IsRequired reflects it — so the returned set with `IsRequired == true` is the required-field minimum for that selection. Fields outside the selection are omitted entirely (see PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.ApplicablePaymentTypes).

position.description: Relative ordering among fields. Fields are returned ordered by this value.

isSecret.description:
Whether the field holds a secret (credential) value. Secret values are encrypted at rest and
are never returned in plaintext; clients should treat secret fields as write-only.

validationRegex.description: Optional regular expression the submitted string value must match.

maxLength.description: Maximum character length for string values. Null means no limit.

validationMessage.description: Human-readable message shown when validation fails. When null, a generic message is generated.

applicablePaymentTypes.description: Payment type names this field applies to — the same tokens as PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorSummaryDto.SupportedPaymentTypes and PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorPaymentTypeRefDto.Name, so a client can correlate a field to a payment type with one consistent token (no side lookup). Null or empty means the field applies to every payment type. When a request scopes the schema to a subset of payment types, fields outside that subset are omitted from the response.

defaultValue.description: Optional default value pre-populated when creating a new processor profile.

ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.description:
Describes a single configuration field that a processor requires when building a
merchant processor profile. Returned by the processor config-schema discovery endpoint
so API clients know which keys to populate, their types, and their validation rules.

value.description: The value to submit for the field when this option is selected. Submit this verbatim.

label.description: The human-friendly label to present for this option.

ProcessorFieldOptionDto.description:
A single selectable option for a closed-set (dropdown) field, as an explicit
`{value, label}` pair. This removes the ambiguity of the legacy parallel
`DropdownList` / `DropdownValues` arrays: a client submits PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldOptionDto.Value
verbatim as the field value and shows PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldOptionDto.Label to an operator.

key.description: The field definition key this result is for.

ok.description: True when the submitted value passed every constraint for this field.

message.description: Human-readable failure detail when PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldValidationResultDto.Ok is false; null when the field passed.

ProcessorFieldValidationResultDto.description: The validation outcome for a single processor configuration field.

key.description: Unique field key used to match with the corresponding processor field definition. Required on input.

name.description:
Human-friendly label for UI display. Optional on input; when omitted, the server fills it from
the matching processor field definition.

rawJson.description:
Raw JSON value stored for the field (the JSON token serialized as a string). Optional on input
when PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorFieldValueDto.Value is supplied instead; the two are kept in sync.

value.description:
The field value as a JSON token. Preferred input form: send the value directly (string, number,
boolean, etc.) and it is round-tripped through PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorFieldValueDto.RawJson.

ProcessorFieldValueDto.description:
A single processor-specific field value within a merchant's processor profile, both on input
(merchant create/update) and output (merchant read).

id.description: Global, environment-independent identifier of the payment type.

when populating a profile's payment types; the server resolves PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorPaymentTypeRefDto.Id from it.

ProcessorPaymentTypeRefDto.description:
A reference to a payment type as an explicit `{id, name}` pair. This is the platform's
standard representation convention for entity references on the processor discovery surface
(closed-set dropdown options use the parallel PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldOptionDto`{value, label}` shape).

Always empty under the open-batch-eligibility predicate (eligible transactions have
no `ProcessorBatchId` stamped). Retained for HTTP-client / generated-SDK
backward compatibility; will be removed in a future major.

transaction-detail routing-decision panel's profile modal). Deliberately distinct from

RateLimitAccumulationType.description: Determines what a rate limiter accumulates per window.
x-enumDescriptions: Counts discrete requests, checked against PermitLimit.
Accumulates a decimal amount (for example a transaction value), checked against MaxAmount. Only FixedWindow supports amount accumulation.

RateLimitAlgorithm.description: The algorithm used to enforce a rate limit.
x-enumDescriptions: Fixed (tumbling) window: the counter resets when the window rolls over. The window identifier is derived from the current UTC instant, so every process agrees on the boundary without coordination.
Sliding window: tracks individual request timestamps over a rolling span using a sorted set. More precise than a fixed window at the cost of more Redis memory.
Token bucket: permits replenish at a steady rate and short bursts are allowed up to the bucket capacity.
Concurrency limiter: bounds the number of concurrent in-flight requests. The slot is held for the duration of the downstream request and released afterwards.

The scope at which a rate limiter operates. Determines the Redis key partitioning

x-enumDescriptions: Platform-wide limit shared across all tenants and merchants.
Per-tenant limit. Keyed by the tenant identifier.
Per-merchant limit. Keyed by the merchant identifier.
Per-entity limit (for example a specific hosted payment page instance). Keyed by the entity identifier supplied by an IRateLimitEntityConfigProvider.

PhoeniXGate.Customers.RecurringBilling.RecurringBillingRunItemDto.TransactionId populated) but the customer document update that
would have written the new `ExecutionHistory` record and advanced
`NextScheduledRun` failed at `SaveChangesAsync`. The charge stands;
the contract's local view of it is missing until the next billing cycle replays
the persistence step (deterministic `IdempotencyKey` prevents re-charge).

distinguish a transient Cosmos concurrency conflict from a structural shape bug
without leaving the page. Null when PhoeniXGate.Customers.RecurringBilling.RecurringBillingRunItemDto.PersistenceFailed is null.

A refund run as a follow-up action against a previously approved and settled original transaction. The refund is a new transaction in its own right and flows through the normal auth + settlement pipeline, but carries a reference to its parent via OriginalTransaction and debits the parent's refund capacity.

SettleFlag.description: Represents the settlement status of a transaction.
x-enumDescriptions: The transaction is open and not yet settled.
The transaction has been successfully settled.
The transaction has been rolled back or reversed.
The transaction is currently in the process of being settled.
The transaction is on hold and cannot be settled at the moment.

SettlementBatchStatus.description: Status of a settlement batch through its lifecycle.
x-enumDescriptions: Batch created, awaiting processor submission.
Batch successfully settled with the processor.
Batch settlement failed.
Some transactions settled, others rejected by the processor.

No transactions were eligible to settle for this (merchant, processor) group. A successful no-op outcome, distinct from Failed (a genuine fault) and from Completed (a real settle). Recorded so a settlement run leaves a history row for every targeted (merchant, processor) even when zero transactions are loaded. The short explanation is carried in SettlementBatch.ErrorMessage as the per-batch outcome detail.

The batch could not be settled automatically and is parked for operator action . Distinct from Failed: a Failed closed batch is re-attempted on the next run (transient fault), whereas an OperatorActionRequired batch is deliberately excluded from automatic retry because blindly re-submitting it would just re-fail. Two causes park a batch here: a non-transient duplicate-batch-number processor rejection (the same processor BatchNumber will keep colliding until an operator bumps it), and exhaustion of SettlementConsts.MaxSettlementRetries transient retries. The batch's transactions are moved to SettlementStatus.SettlementOnHold so they stop auto-retrying; the reason is carried in SettlementBatch.ErrorMessage. The operator UI (follow-up story) lists these and can retry with a bumped processor BatchNumber.

The batch was not submitted because a concurrent settlement run already held the terminal lock for the same (Fiserv MerchID, TermID) pair (UMF Appendix M 42.1: only one batch at a time per terminal). Distinct from Failed: nothing went wrong, this run simply deferred to the run that already owned the terminal. The next scheduled run retries normally.

runDateUtc.description:
When the settlement run that produced this batch was kicked off (`SettlementBatch.RunDate`).
This is the batch's "Run Date" display value, not its completion time.

completedAtUtc.description:
When the batch first reached a terminal outcome (`SettlementBatch.CompletedAtUtc`).
Null for legacy batches created before the field existed, or a batch still in flight.

duration.description:
The settlement-attempt duration: PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchSummaryDto.CompletedAtUtc minus the batch's audit
creation time, computed server-side via `SettlementDurationCalculator` (clamped at zero).
Null when PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchSummaryDto.CompletedAtUtc is null. Derived from per-batch set-once timestamps so
it is immune to later batch mutations (re-settle, park, backfill, override).

settledCount.description:
Number of items that successfully settled. Equals PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchSummaryDto.TotalTransactionCount
for fully successful batches; less for PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchStatus.PartiallyCompleted.
Null for legacy batches and batches still PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchStatus.Pending.

processorKey.description:
The lower-cased processor key the batch was produced for (the same key the settlement
close fans out on). Needed by the operator retry action to target the re-settle engine
entrypoint at the correct (merchant, processor) counter. Null for legacy batches created
before the key was persisted. Non-sensitive: a short identifier such as `tsys`.

gatewayBatchId.description:
The gateway batch id this run settled (`SettlementBatch.OpenBatchId`). Identifies the
single batch the operator retry resubmits. Null for legacy batches created before the id

succeeded.description: True when the override was applied and persisted.

skipReason.description:
Stable diagnostic code populated when PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementOverrideAttemptResult.Succeeded is false. Values are

SettlementOverrideAttemptResult.description:
Per-transaction outcome of a M:PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.ITransactionSettlementOverrideAppService.OverrideAsync(PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementOverrideRequestDto)

transactionIds.description: The transactions to apply the override to. 1–200 ids per request.

Request payload for an admin-driven manual settlement-status override. Designed

SettlementStatus.description: Settlement status for transactions requiring processor settlement
x-enumDescriptions: Transaction is waiting to be settled with the processor
Settlement completed successfully with the processor
Settlement failed - requires review and retry (rollback)
Transaction is not eligible for settlement (voided, reversed, or not yet captured)
Settlement is currently in progress with the processor.
Settlement is on hold and cannot proceed at the moment.
Settlement was rolled back or reversed after a completed attempt. Distinct from SettlementFailed which indicates a transient failure needing retry.

A reversal was attempted but the processor did not confirm that the authorization hold was voided — the contributor saw a non-Ok result code (transport failure, timeout, swallowed exception, malformed response, etc.). Distinct from NotEligible (a confirmed reversal/void) and SettlementFailed (a settlement-time failure). Operations need to confirm the hold state with the processor and reverse manually if required. The transaction's Stage is left at the pre-reversal value; the close-stage history entry is NOT written.

reason.description: Free-text justification supplied by the operator. Required, trimmed, 5-500 chars.

operatorUserId.description: The user id of the operator who applied the override.

operatorUserName.description:
The display name of the operator at the time of the override (snapshot — does not
follow rename of the underlying user account).

overriddenAt.description: UTC timestamp the override was applied.

SettlementStatusOverrideRecord.description:
A single audit record for an admin-driven manual override of a transaction's
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.SettlementStatus. Records are appended to
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.OverrideHistory by the
`Transaction.OverrideSettlementStatus` domain method and rendered on the
transaction detail page so subsequent admins can see who changed the settlement
state, when, why, and from what value.


All value-type properties are nullable so existing Cosmos documents that gain
an Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.OverrideHistory entry from an older code
path (or are deserialised by a future shape-mismatched build) do not fail
deserialisation. New records are always written with all fields populated; UI
and audit code should treat null fields on a persisted record as a corrupt
document and surface accordingly rather than papering over it.

SmsConsentCaptureMethod.description:
How a consent or opt-out record came to be. Part of the proof-of-consent evidence retained per the
Twilio Messaging Policy record-keeping requirement, and useful for triage when a recipient disputes
having opted in or out.
x-enumDescriptions: Capture method was not supplied. Treated as the least-authoritative evidence.
Recipient opted in through a public web form (e.g. a hosted checkout consent checkbox).
An operator captured consent while taking the payment in the Virtual Terminal.
Consent was captured on a Hosted Payment Page flow.
The record was created from a bulk import of prior consent evidence.
Consent or opt-out was recorded through the API by an integrating system.
An administrator recorded the consent or opt-out manually.

Opt-out was back-filled from a carrier send-time signal (Twilio error 21610 on send). The platform learned of the revocation from the carrier rather than capturing it directly. Inbound STOP / START replies use InboundKeyword instead, which keeps a more precise evidence trail.

Consent transition was captured from an inbound SMS keyword the recipient texted to the platform number (STOP / UNSUBSCRIBE / START / etc.), received on the Twilio inbound webhook. The inbound message SID is retained as the evidence reference.

phoneNumber.description: The E.164-normalized number the check was resolved against. Empty when the input could not be normalized.

merchantId.description: Merchant scope the check was evaluated in.

hasRecord.description: `true` when a consent record exists for this number in scope.

isOptedOut.description: `true` when the recipient has opted out — the SMS channel should be disabled.

canSendSms.description: `true` when a send is currently allowed by the consent store. This is the inverse of PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsConsentCheckResultDto.IsOptedOut: no record and opted-in both allow. (Whether express consent is required before the first send is a caller policy decision, not enforced here.)

SmsConsentCheckResultDto.description:
Result of a send-time pre-check: whether SMS may be sent to a phone number for a merchant scope.
A send UI uses this to disable the SMS channel for an opted-out recipient before the operator sends
(e.g. the invoice pay-link send dialog).

phoneNumber.description: Canonical E.164 phone number this record governs.

merchantId.description: Merchant the record is scoped to.

statusChangedAt.description: When the current status was last set (UTC).

evidenceText.description: Proof-of-consent evidence for the current status.

evidenceReference.description: Stable reference for the current status's source.

history.description: Append-only audit trail of every status transition, oldest first.

SmsConsentDto.description: Read-only DTO for a merchant-scoped SMS consent / opt-out record, including its audit history.

evidenceReference.description: Stable reference tying this transition to its source.

SmsConsentHistoryEntryDto.description: Read-only DTO for one entry in a PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsConsentDto's audit trail.

SmsConsentStatus.description: Consent / opt-out state of a phone number for a single (tenant, merchant) scope.
x-enumDescriptions: The recipient has expressly consented to receive SMS from this merchant. Sends are allowed.
The recipient has revoked consent (STOP keyword, carrier unsubscribe, or an operator action). The send-time gate blocks every SMS to this number for this merchant until a re-opt-in is recorded.

SmsDeliveryStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a single outbound SMS, as recorded on its `SmsEvents` row. The first three
values are gateway-side outcomes stamped by the platform at send time; the rest arrive later on
Twilio status callbacks.
x-enumDescriptions: No state recorded. Only ever seen on a malformed document.

The send-time compliance gate refused the message (for example the recipient has opted out). No Twilio API call was made, so no carrier callback will ever follow. Distinct from GatewaySendFailed so a compliance block is auditable separately from a carrier fault.
The Twilio API rejected the create-message call. The message never entered the carrier network.
Twilio accepted the message. Carrier callbacks (if a status callback URL was set) follow.
Carrier callback: the message is queued, accepted, scheduled, or sending.
Carrier callback: the message has been handed to the carrier.
Carrier callback: the carrier confirmed delivery to the handset.
Carrier callback: the carrier could not deliver the message. Usually carries a Twilio error code.
Carrier callback: the message failed outright or was cancelled. Usually carries a Twilio error code.

SmsInboundKeyword.description:
Classification of an inbound SMS the platform received on its Twilio number. Drives whether an
inbound message records a consent transition (opt-out / opt-in), returns a branded informational
reply (help), or is simply persisted for operator review (none).
x-enumDescriptions: Not a recognized keyword. The message is persisted for operator review; no consent change.
An opt-out keyword (STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, OPTOUT, CANCEL, END, REVOKE, QUIT).
An opt-in / re-subscribe keyword (START, UNSTOP, YES).
The HELP keyword: the recipient asked for program identification and a support contact.

correlationId.description:
The platform correlation id for this message. Equal to Volo.Abp.Application.Dtos.EntityDto`1.Id: there is
exactly one row per outbound message, so the correlation id is the document key. Surfaced under
its own name because that is what callers of the send API hold.

toPhoneNumberMasked.description: Recipient reduced to its last four digits (for example `•••••••4567`).

fromPhoneNumberMasked.description: Sending number reduced to its last four digits, when the send used a from-number.

messagingServiceSid.description: The Messaging Service SID the send routed through, when one was configured.

messageSid.description: Twilio's message SID, once the API accepted the message. Null for blocked / failed sends.

isFailure.description: Whether PhoeniXGate.Twilio.SmsLog.SmsLogDto.Status means the message did not reach the handset.

twilioErrorCode.description: Twilio numeric error code from the failing send or callback, when one was reported.

failureCode.description: Platform error code explaining a gateway-side refusal (for example a compliance block).

bodyLength.description: Message length in characters. The body itself is never stored or returned.

lastStatusAt.description: When the most recent carrier callback was applied (UTC). Null until the first one lands.

tenantId.description: Tenant the message was sent under.

merchantId.description: Merchant the message belongs to.

SmsLogDto.description: Read-only projection of one outbound SMS delivery-log row.

SmsMessageCategory.description:
Compliance category of an outbound SMS. Carried on `SmsMessage.Properties` (see
PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsMessageProperties) so the send-time gate and the content / quiet-hours policy
(PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsContentPolicy) can distinguish message classes.
x-enumDescriptions: Transactional message tied to a specific interaction the recipient initiated or expects (payment link, receipt, invoice, one-time passcode). This is the platform's default when a caller sets no category: every SMS sender wired today is transactional.

Promotional / marketing message. Requires express marketing consent and is subject to the stricter content and timing policy. Callers sending marketing SMS must set this explicitly; it is never inferred.

Recurring reminder in an ongoing program the recipient enrolled in (an overdue-invoice reminder series, a scheduled payment nudge). Not marketing, but recurring, so CTIA requires the opt-out instruction to ride on the message itself and TCPA timing applies.

SoftDescriptor.description: Represents a soft descriptor for a transaction, containing alternative merchant information.

SpecialCondition.description:
Visa/Mastercard "special condition" tag for transactions that need network-specific
handling beyond standard purchase semantics. Maps to TSYS `SpecialConditionIndicator`
(and the equivalent indicators on other processor networks).
x-enumDescriptions: No special condition applies — standard purchase semantics.

Quasi-cash purchase: a transaction that resembles cash equivalent (money orders, foreign currency, traveler's cheques, gaming chips, casino vouchers, etc.). Triggers TSYS SpecialConditionIndicator=8 and requires a populated CardholderId on the network request.

Quasi-MOTO: a card-present capture that the merchant is required to process under MOTO routing rules (e.g. cert scenarios, specific Visa product types). Distinct from QuasiCash — the merchant remains in retail context but presence flags flip to MOTO for network routing.

SplitTenderRole.description:
Identifies a transaction's position within a split-tender group: the set of transactions that
together collect one order total after a partial approval left a shortfall.
x-enumDescriptions: The first tender in the group: the transaction whose partial approval created the shortfall. Exactly one member of a group holds this role, and it always carries SplitTenderSequence = 1.

A follow-up tender collecting part of the remaining balance. A group may hold several, ordered by SplitTenderSequence (2, 3, ...). A continuation can itself be partially approved, which starts the disposition cycle again.

Merchant-triggered charges for pre-agreed events (balance top-ups, usage overages, no-show fees, delayed charges). Maps to several MIT reason codes including UnscheduledCOF, NoShow, DelayedCharge, and IncrementalAuth.
A single known future cardholder-initiated purchase the credential was saved for (e.g. "save card for my next order"). Not used for MITs.
